item.title: Pier & Beam August Happy Hour / 2026 Future Landmark Celebration
item.description:
Thursday, August 27, 2026 at 6 PM

Location: JW Marriott Houston Downtown, 806 Main Street, Houston, TX, 77002

Each year, the Future Landmark Award recognizes an outstanding Houston building or place completed within the past decade — a project that combines architectural excellence with a lasting contribution to its neighborhood and to the city. After weeks of nominations and voting by Pier & Beam members, we'll reveal this year's winner during a presentation at 6:45 p.m.

From Preservation Houston

item.title: Woodland Heights Architecture Walk
item.description:
Sunday, September 13, 2026 at 6 PM

Architecture Walks begin at 6 p.m. in June, July, August and September.The William A. Wilson Realty Co. began developing Woodland Heights in 1907 on 136 acres of land that was once part of John Austin's Mexican land grant. The neighborhood was one of Houston's first "streetcar suburbs" — a streetcar line ran from downtown along Houston Avenue to just outside the Woodland Heights gates, enabling working-class Houstonians to live in a lovely wooded setting and easily commute to their jobs.

From Preservation Houston

item.title: Historic Glenwood Cemetery Part II walking tour: Houston After Oil
item.description:
Saturday, September 26, 2026 at 10 AM

Please note that advance ticket purchase is required for this tour.Glenwood Cemetery, established in 1871 on rolling, wooded land near Buffalo Bayou, is one of the most beautiful outdoor spaces in Houston. It is also the resting place of scores of people who built Houston into the city we know today. This two-hour docent-guided tour looks at the lives and legacies of some of the men and women buried at Glenwood who shaped Houston after the turn of the 20th century.

From Preservation Houston

item.title: 2026 Good Brick Tour
item.description:
Saturday, November 7, 2026 at 12 PM

Save the date for Preservation Houston's 2026 Good Brick Tour, returning Saturday and Sunday, November 7 and 8. Now in its 13th year, this annual self-guided tour offers a rare opportunity to step inside some of Houston's most remarkable historic places and experience the city's architectural heritage firsthand.
